criteria_note: Scored A-F, G, X1, U1, U2 (summary-specific). R1-R3, T1-T3, S1 do not apply. Prose length counts body characters without front matter, headings, display math, tables, images and references (inline math and spaces kept). The tavily extractor failed (quota), so the arXiv HTML was fetched with curl and converted to text for the claim check.

A.reason: Standard five-part arc and clean markup. The section '## 구현 방식' (l.42) holds the evaluation-time reward normalization (l.44) and tool-call statistics (l.46), not implementation: no training algorithm, backbone training data or ToolScale pipeline, so the heading does not match its contents.

B.reason: Mostly natural 입니다 register. Transliteration '오프더셸프(off-the-shelf)' (l.23, l.29) reads as a calque; '기성 모델' would be the natural word. Inconsistent notation: 'τ²-Bench' (l.17, l.46) vs '$$\tau^{2}$$-Bench' (l.23). Formulaic lead-ins: '최종 보상은 다음과 같습니다.' (l.33), 'τ²-Bench에서 비교 대상별 점수와 비용, 지연은 다음과 같습니다.' (l.52).

C.reason: l.29 restates the TL;DR almost word for word ('언제, 어떻게 부를지 정하고, 그 결과를 여러 턴에 걸쳐 조합'). l.31 introduces HLE again ('Humanity's Last Exam(HLE)이라는 고난도 추론 벤치마크') after l.21 already defined it. l.44 jumps to the evaluation reward right after the training reward without saying why. l.62 files the preference test under '학습 때 본 적 없는 조건', which it is not.

D.reason: Good help where it is hard: the preference-vector reading (l.38) and the batch min-max worked example (l.40, numerically right: the cheap trajectory gets 1 and the expensive one 0). The illustrative trajectory is labelled hypothetical (l.31). FRAMES and τ²-Bench are never explained.

E.reason: The τ²-Bench table (l.54-58) copies Table 16 cells. The second table (l.64-69) puts two different experiments, unseen tools (Table 2) and the preference reward (Table 3), into one table whose columns mean different things per row. The main multi-benchmark comparison (Table 1) is missing, so FRAMES accuracy is never given in numbers. The figure sits next to its discussion (l.73-75).

F.reason: All 20 checked claims are supported, including the Table 15/16/2/3 cells and the derived ratios (52.8/10.3 > 5x at l.60). Minor: l.83 suggests checking retraining needs 'if the price structure changes a lot' without mentioning that the paper already tests an unseen pricing configuration (Appendix H); this is framed as advice, not as missing work.

G.reason: use_math is set and $$ is used throughout; display math has blank lines around it; description is 127 characters, opens with 'ToolOrchestra', and its numbers (37.1, 35.1, 2.5x) are all in the TL;DR; no Liquid; the file is not checked against the blog lint here.

X1.reason: Seven tags. 'Multi-Objective-Reward' and 'Cost-Aware-Reinforcement-Learning' do not appear in the paper (the human-fix item flags exactly this), and 'Synthetic-Tool-Use-Data' names data synthesis, which the post never discusses.

U1.reason: Motivation, reward and results are covered, but a reader would not learn that ToolScale, the automatically synthesized verifiable multi-turn dataset across 10 domains, is a core contribution and the training data (it is never mentioned). Also missing: GRPO, the Qwen3-8B backbone and the training setup. FRAMES gets no numbers (l.50: '큰 차이로 앞서는데').

U2.reason: The TL;DR (l.17) runs to five sentences, more than 'two-to-three lines'. The headline numbers repeat at l.17 and l.50. The limitation (l.83) is the writer's own reading ('상한을 넘어섰다기보다 강한 모델을 적게 부르는 방식'), not grounded in the paper. Length suits a five-minute read.

claim_headings.evidence: All headings are generic labels: '연구 배경', '제안 방법', '구현 방식', '실험 결과', '의의와 한계' (l.19-77).

mechanism_reason_formula_example.evidence: Reward mechanism (l.33) leads to the outcome gate (l.35-38), the formula, and the worked example (l.40).

facts_said_once.evidence: 37.1/35.1/2.5x/30% appear at l.17 and l.50; the orchestrator's role at l.17 and l.29; HLE is defined at l.21 and l.31.

numbers_with_variant_scope_unit.evidence: The τ²-Bench table gives no units for cost and latency (l.54); the cost 34.8 vs 81.3 (l.71) has no unit; call counts (l.46) give their scope.

nothing_invented.evidence: All checked claims are supported; the hypothetical examples are labelled (l.31, l.40).

D.reason: Benchmarks are glossed at first use (l.17). The worked example (l.37: 1/1 + 30/10 = 4) is correct for Eq.5. The sign explanation (l.31) helps but rests on negative weights the paper does not allow, and the training reward, the hard part, gets no explanation.
